title: Introduce credential middleware and canonical async-stream shape across SDKs
author: Oliver Kwan
release_notes: Introduce a middleware-based credential surface and align async streaming shapes across Python/TS/Go SDKs. Provides a migration shim for existing token hooks and bumps SDK versions: python v1.13.0, typescript v2.8.0, go v1.6.2. No breaking behavior expected; minor rename shims included.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight credential middleware abstraction and a canonical async-stream shape (pullstream async iterator / async generator alignment) implemented across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: developers have been integrating bespoke token refresh hooks per language which led to subtle inconsistencies in retry semantics and stream resume behavior. This work unifies the shape so application code and examples can be shared across languages, and introduces a middleware-level credential orchestrator that centralizes token lookup/fallthrough and prefetching.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced `CredentialMiddleware` (conceptual name) implemented in each SDK. The middleware exposes a small interface for: get(), refresh_if_needed(), and attach_to_request(). Backed by language-specific adapters but with consistent semantics.
- Canonicalized async stream shape: Pull-based async iterator in TS/Py and a thin channel/iterator facade in Go. Normalized APIs for pause/resume, checkpoint tokens, and error surfaces so cross-language examples are identical.
- Retry ergonomics: unified retry presets added (idempotent vs streaming-friendly profiles) and applied to streaming calls by default. Streaming retries now respect credential refresh windows and will trigger a graceful stream reattach flow rather than immediate error propagation for transient auth failures.
- Migration shims: kept legacy token hooks (on_token_refresh, token_provider) and provided adapters to the new middleware so existing integrations continue to work without changes. A deprecation plan with warnings is in place.
- Tests and telemetry: added end-to-end integration tests that run against the local mock gateway for token rotation scenarios and CI integration tests to validate continuations across reconnects. Updated telemetry hooks to emit credential refresh events for SLO correlation.

Commits (summary):
- c1a3e8a: introduce common middleware interface docs and design notes
- d4f2b9f: implement python credential middleware and async-generator adapter for pullstream shape
- e5b3c12: add ts middleware and adjust async-iterable shim; bump ts SDK to v2.8.0
- f8c7d21: implement go credential orchestrator and iterator facade; bump go SDK to v1.6.2
- b2a6e7d: add migration shims, deprecation warnings, and comprehensive unit/integration tests
- 7c3fd44: ci: flake fixes and test timeouts tuned for slow CI workers

Files changed (representative):
- python/redwood_sdk/auth/middleware.py (new)
- python/redwood_sdk/stream/pullstream.py (refactor)
- typescript/src/credential/middleware.ts (new)
- typescript/src/stream/pull-iterable.ts (refactor)
- go/sdk/cred/middleware.go (new)
- go/sdk/stream/iter_facade.go (new)
- shared/docs/sdk/credential-middleware.md (new design doc)
- tests/e2e/cred_rotation.test.ts (new)

Design notes / rationale:
- Middleware boundary: By elevating credential logic to middleware we separate policy (when/how to refresh) from transport (how to attach tokens to requests). This makes adding side features like prefetch/lease or HSM-backed retrievals possible without changing stream logic.
- Canonical stream shape: After reviewing usage patterns across customer examples and internal libs we converged on a pull-based async iterator as the canonical shape because it composes nicely with backpressure and reconnect semantics. Go uses a minimal channel-backed iterator to match ergonomic expectations of the language.

Testing and CI:
- CI matrix updated to run Python 3.10/3.11, Node 18/20, and Go 1.20/1.21 job permutations for the SDKs.
- Added a flaky-tolerant harness for the e2e token rotation tests (they sometimes hit timing races in CI).
- All checks currently passing in this branch: unit, lint, typecheck, integration-e2e.

Review discussion (high level):
- Aisha: "Can we make the refresh window configurable per-client? Some customers rotate tokens aggressively."
  - Oliver: "Yes — middleware accepts an optional policy; default is conservative. Added configuration tests and docs."
- Benji: "TS typing ergonomics look good but prefer a lighter-weight adapter for browser clients."
  - Oliver: "Added a browser adapter that omits node-only deps and a small example in examples/ts/browser.md."
- Clara: "Is there a risk that automatic reattach masks real auth failures and hides real errors from users?"
  - Oliver: "We only auto-reattach on transient codes (401 with refresh window, 429 in streaming with retryable profile); all other errors surface immediately. Added explicit telemetry for silent reattach so users can audit."

Migration notes for consumers:
- No immediate breaking changes. If you rely on legacy token hooks, your code will continue to work via the adapter but you will see a deprecation warning in logs.
- Recommended path: move to the middleware configuration so you can take advantage of prefetch and the unified retry profiles. Example migration snippets are added to shared/docs/sdk/credential-middleware.md.

Performance and metrics:
- End-to-end benchmarks against our local serving runtime show negligible added latency (~+1ms median) and a modest reduction in failed-stream RPS during token rotation windows (improvement ~18%).

Changelog / release bump:
- python SDK bumped to v1.13.0
- typescript SDK bumped to v2.8.0
- go SDK bumped to v1.6.2

Merge strategy: squash-and-merge. Post-merge actions: cut SDK releases, publish migration docs to the SDK docs site, and create a follow-up ticket ENG-2193 to run a customer-facing migration bake.

Notes: This PR stitches work across three SDKs and required coordinating lint/test updates in each language subrepo. Kept changes small per-file but pervasive in scope (middleware + stream shape).
